subject: Clarify Redwood default visibility / retention for requests, prompts, and outputs
messages:

Subject: Quick clarifications on what Redwood keeps by default (requests/outputs/prompts)

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security team is finalizing the data handling section of the SOW and we need a concise description of Redwood's default "visibility" window for different artifacts. Specifically:

1) What you store by default for a standard hosted API call (request payload, response text, prompts, tool outputs, embeddings).
2) How long each artifact is retained before automatic purge.
3) Whether we can opt-out per-request (headers/API) vs. tenant-level configuration.
4) What the deletion workflow looks like if we request immediate purge (audit trail, time-to-purge).
5) Residency options for EU data — is there any difference in retention policy or purge behavior?

Can you send a short example we can drop into our security questionnaire? Ideally one paragraph + a short bulleted table.

Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise description you can paste into the questionnaire plus a short example matrix. Happy to sync if you want us to tailor wording for a legal or procurement doc.

One-paragraph summary you can use:
Redwood captures minimal request and runtime artifacts by default to operate the hosted inference service. By default, full request and response payloads (raw request body and generated text) are retained for 30 days to support debugging, incident investigation, and quality monitoring. Derived artifacts such as summarized outputs and function/tool call traces are retained for 60 days. Short-lived derivatives (temporary KV cache entries, session tokens) are ephemeral and removed within 7 days. Customers can opt out of storage for individual calls using our per-request header or change tenant retention settings in the console; deletion requests are recorded in an audit log and purge jobs complete within 72 hours unless a legal hold is in place. EU-region customers may elect EU-only residency for storage and purges; residency choice does not change the default retention durations but affects the physical location of retained data.

Quick retention matrix (example):
- Raw request payload: 30 days (default)
- Generated response text (full outputs): 60 days
- Prompt history / prompt fragments: 30 days
- Embeddings and ranking artifacts: 14 days (derived vector store entries are automatically pruned)
- KV cache / session artifacts: ephemeral (up to 7 days)

Opt-out options:
- Per-request: set header "Prefer: no-store" or X-Redwood-No-Store: 1 to prevent that call from being persisted.
- Tenant-level: Admins can change retention profile in Redwood Console (Compliance -> Data Controls) to reduce or disable capture; changes apply prospectively.

Deletion workflow:
- Customer files a deletion request via Console or Support ticket.
- System marks relevant records for purge and creates an immutable audit entry.
- Background purge runs and completes within 72 hours (usually under 24 hours for small datasets).
- If data is subject to legal hold, purge is paused and the customer is notified.

EU residency note:
- Selecting EU-only residency routes storage and backups to EU regions and running purge jobs in-region. Retention durations remain configurable but default values are the same across regions.

Attaching a short PDF summary and CSV examples that map artifact names to retention windows.

Thanks Jordan — this is really helpful. Couple of quick follow-ups from our data-protection team:

1) "Prompt history" is sometimes ambiguous for us. If a customer sends a multi-turn conversation, what exactly counts as prompt fragments vs. generated output? For example, if we send a user message and then the assistant reply, is the user message treated as a stored prompt or part of the request?
2) Embeddings: if we request on-the-fly embeddings for a user document, are vectors retained in any long-term store by default or just cached briefly?
3) If we enable "no-store" header on a call that triggers a function/tool call (e.g., code execution or web fetch), does Redwood still keep function outputs for debugging?

We want to make sure the answers are precise for our questionnaire.

- Liam

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on what Redwood keeps by default (requests/outputs/prompts)

Liam —

Great questions. Short, precise answers you can paste into the DPA/security questionnaire below.

1) Prompt vs. output definition:
- "Prompt" = the user-provided input(s) and any system messages we receive as part of the request (this includes prior user turns sent as context).
- "Generated output" = text produced by the model (assistant reply) and any structured function/tool responses produced by the runtime.
So in a multi-turn chat, each user message you send is considered a prompt fragment; the assistant reply is a generated output. Both are captured according to the matrix above unless a no-store header is used.

2) Embeddings retention:
- On-the-fly embedding calls are not stored persistently by default in a long-term vector DB. Embeddings may be cached short-term (up to 14 days) to improve repeated-call performance, but they are not added to durable customer vector indexes unless you explicitly save them via the embedding-index APIs. Tenant settings control whether transient embedding caches are kept beyond default windows.

3) No-store header interaction with function/tool calls:
- Per-call no-store prevents Redwood from persisting the request/response and generated output to long-term logs and telemetry. However, short-lived function traces needed to execute the call (for example, call payloads to connectors) may still be available transiently in in-memory runtime traces for debugging; those traces are removed within the ephemeral window (<= 7 days). If you need zero retention for tool outputs, use tenant-level settings plus no-store and notify Support so we can disable connector-level retention for your tenant.

If you like, we can convert this into a one-page Q&A PDF with the exact text your legal team prefers. Also included here is a shared Drive link to the short CSV mapping we attached earlier.

Cheers,
Jordan
